author: patrick-schultz
body:
## Change Description

The bulk of the changes are in the files `BlockMatrixType.scala`, `MatrixSparsity.scala`, and `LowerBlockMatrixIR.scala`. I suggest starting with those, with the summaries below.

I acknowledge this is a big change containing a lot of non-trivial logic. Please do ask for explanations and clarifications.

### BlockMatrixType and MatrixSparsity
`BlockMatrixType` has a `sparsity`, of type `BlockMatrixSparsity`, which is either dense or a set of present blocks. In this PR I've moved the sparsity representation to `MatrixSparsity`, which is a generic encoding of the sparsity pattern of a sparse matrix. For a `BlockMatrixType`, the sparsity will be a `nBlockRows` by `nBlockCols` `MatrixSparsity`.

Besides moving `BlockMatrixSparsity` to `MatrixSparsity`, and removing references to blocks, the encoding of the sparsity is also streamlined. Before, `BlockMatrixSparsity` held an array of coordinates of present blocks, in an arbitrary order. Methods that need the present blocks in a particular order (usually column major) would need to sort them, and we also built a `Set` of present blocks to handle the `isPresent` query.

Now, `MatrixSparsity` (in the sparse case) enforces that the array of present blocks is always in column major order. This simplifies some of the logic, and lets us handle `isPresent` with binary search (similarly for unions/intersections of sparsity, which now take advantage of the ordering).

In addition, `MatrixSparsity` now knows its dimensions, which `BlockMatrixSparsity` did not. 

I've also gotten rid of all the complicated methods on the CSC (compressed sparse column) encoding (e.g. `transposeCSCSparsity`). Instead, I do all the transformations on the simple coordinate list encoding, and convert to CSC as late as possible.

### LowerBlockMatrixIR
The changes in this file are mostly about a redesign of the `BMSContexts` class. `BMSContexts` bundles together a runtime array of context values (similar to the contexts for a `TableStage`), with a representation of the sparsity pattern, which conceptually maps each context value to the coordinates of its block.

Before, the sparsity pattern was also encoded by runtime values. In the sparse case, this used runtime arrays `rowPos` and `rowIdx` using a CSC encoding. Working with this encoding created a lot of non-trivial runtime logic. But sparsity is completely known at compile time, so all this runtime logic was unnecessary.

There are still cases where we need to work with a CSC encoding of the sparsity at runtime. These cases are now handled by the class `DynamicBMSContexts`, which is essentially the same as the old `BMSContexts`, but now has a minimal interface of three methods. Importantly, these methods are only about consuming a block matrix, not transforming to a new one (like transpose).

The new `BMSContexts` now pairs a statically known `MatrixSparsity` with a `DynamicBMSContexts`. The big change from before is that all methods that produce a new `BMSContexts` now handle all the sparsity logic at compile time, and simply embed the new sparsity in the IR using literals. This typically requires us to also embed an array of ints mapping from old to new positions in the contexts array, which we use at runtime to reorder the contexts as needed.

## Security Assessment

- This change cannot impact the Hail Batch instance as deployed by Broad Institute in GCP

author: ak2000
body:
## Summary
With the move to asyncio, agents need not be spawned in another thread or process from the script. This PR introduces the ability to run an agent in the current asyncio event loop. This was suggested by @benclifford in PR #239 as a mechanism needed when launching agents within agents.

This PR woroks by allowing an executor in the `Manager._executors` attribute to be None. This does not change the default behavior of the Manager.launch or any other method --- you must explicitly pass `executors=None` or pass a dictionary with `{name: None}` to get this behavior.

### Why?
CLI tools run via `pnpx` benefit significantly from bundling:
- Single optimized file loads faster than multiple module resolution
- Smaller install size improves download time
- Tree-shaking eliminates unused code from dependencies

# Overview

Addresses #4704.

**This PR is based on #4806 and should merge after it (after a rebase).**

## What problem does this address?

~We automatically apply a multi-source warning to tables whose metadata claim more than one data source.
A subset of these tables are multi-source because they are _harvested_, which requires some additional considerations by users.~ <-- that was the original aim, but the new one is: Users frequently ask about discrepancies between harvested tables and the raw data, let's see if actually labeling tables affected by harvesting helps! Lots more discussion + analysis in the issue thread for the curious.

## What did you change?

* Add a usage warning for harvested tables.
* Install the harvested warning on tables flagged as harvested in [the metadata tracking sheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1Hv82QN5mVKieRC8B34LxQIsWw3WMjfkarRLgIfvYLX8/edit?gid=120132036#gid=120132036)
* Do a downstream search from those 8 tables to see if columns with the same names show up. If a table has three or more columns that may have come from a harvest table, flag it as well.
* Add appropriate explanatory text to Additional Details for the initial 8 harvest tables
* Add complimentary explanatory text to Additional Details for the downstream tables
* Add a data dictionary page for usage warnings, and explain more of the harvesting details there.
* Centralize utilities for harvest-releated additional details text and description dict wrangling in `pudl.metadata.resource_helpers`

body:
Addresses five issues in meeting tracking, goal display, and student progress views: meetings defaulting to 12pm caused incorrect upcoming/past classification, logged meetings were auto-completed instead of requiring advisor confirmation, action items and notes were truncated in advisor view, and the "Review Active Goals" view showed "No deadline" repeatedly instead of actual goal text. ## Meeting Date Precision Removed time component from meeting dates - now operates at day-level precision: ```javascript // Before: defaulted to noon, causing morning meetings to appear as "upcoming" const scheduledDateTime = new Date(`${formData.scheduledDate}T12:00:00`); // After: midnight local time for consistent day-level comparisons const scheduledDateTime = new Date(`${formData.scheduledDate}T00:00:00`); ``` Updated all date comparisons in `meetingsService.js` to normalize to midnight before comparison. ## Meeting Attendance Workflow Changed logged meetings to require advisor confirmation: - Student-logged meetings: `status='scheduled'`, `attendanceMarked=false` (previously auto-completed) - "Needs Attention" tab: shows all unconfirmed meetings regardless of date - "Past" tab: only shows meetings where `attendanceMarked=true` - "Upcoming" tab: excludes manual logs awaiting confirmation ## Expandable Content in Advisor Views Added expand/collapse for action items and notes in `AdvisorStudentDetail`: - Section-level toggles (Show All/Show Less) when >5 items - Individual note expansion for content >150 chars - Uses ChevronUp/ChevronDown icons ## Goal Display Fixed "Review Active Goals" to display actual goal text: ```javascript // Before: showed title (often undefined) with "No deadline" fallback

{goal.title}

{formatDate(goal.targetDate)} // After: shows actual goal content, removed timeline display

{goal.text || goal.title}

``` Removed unused Calendar imports and formatDate function since goals lack deadlines. ## Student "Need Help" Clarity Improved action item help request labeling: shows "Need Help" when unflagged, "Help Requested" when flagged (previously both states showed "Need Help").

## Description

This pull request introduces a configuration enhancement that adds support for specifying the authentication service URL across all environments in the config/config.js file. With this update, the application can dynamically retrieve the authentication service endpoint through the AUTH_SERVICE_URL environment variable, ensuring consistent behavior in development, testing, and production setups.

Specifically, the following changes were made:

Development environment: Added AUTH_SERVICE_URL, sourced from the AUTH_SERVICE_URL environment variable.

Test environment: Added AUTH_SERVICE_URL, sourced from the AUTH_SERVICE_URL environment variable.

Production environment: Added AUTH_SERVICE_URL, sourced from the AUTH_SERVICE_URL environment variable.

This change improves flexibility in managing authentication configurations and supports seamless integration with different deployment environments.

## Goal

The goal of this update is to centralize and standardize the configuration of the authentication service URL across all environments. By referencing the value from environment variables, developers and deployment pipelines can easily manage authentication endpoints without modifying code, improving maintainability and deployment consistency.

## Impact

This update simplifies environment configuration and enhances deployment flexibility. It does not introduce breaking changes or affect existing functionality. All environments now support dynamic configuration of the authentication service URL, ensuring compatibility with the external authentication microservice introduced in previous updates.

author: dguido
body:
## Summary

Fixes #14846 - Resolves Scaleway deployment failure caused by broken `scaleway_organization_info` Ansible module.

## Problem

The `scaleway_organization_info` module from ansible-collections/community.general is broken and returns empty data (`[]`) when called. This is due to the module using a deprecated API endpoint. See upstream issue: ansible-collections/community.general#3782

When users attempted to deploy to Scaleway, they encountered:
```
[ERROR]: Task failed: Module failed: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'get'
Origin: /roles/cloud-scaleway/tasks/main.yml:6:7
```

This occurred because the role tried to access `scaleway_org.scaleway_organization_info[0]['id']` on an empty list.

## Solution

Instead of relying on the broken Ansible module, this PR:

1. **Prompts users for their Organization/Project ID** - Added a clear prompt with instructions on where to find this in the Scaleway console
2. **Uses Scaleway Marketplace API** - Replaces broken `scaleway_image_info` module with direct API call to the public Marketplace API
3. **Migrates to modern `project` parameter** - Updates `scaleway_compute` calls to use `project` instead of deprecated `organization` parameter
4. **Supports environment variable** - Allows setting `SCW_DEFAULT_ORGANIZATION_ID` to skip the prompt

## Technical Details

- Scaleway's default Project ID equals the Organization ID
- The Marketplace API (`api-marketplace.scaleway.com`) is public and doesn't require authentication
- The `project` parameter was added to `scaleway_compute` in community.general 4.3.0
- This approach matches how other cloud providers (like DigitalOcean) handle similar situations in Algo

## Changes

### Modified Files
- `roles/cloud-scaleway/tasks/prompts.yml` - Added organization/project ID prompt
- `roles/cloud-scaleway/tasks/main.yml` - Removed broken modules, added Marketplace API lookup, updated to use `project` parameter
- `tests/unit/test_scaleway_fix.py` - Added 4 new unit tests

### Testing

**Unit Tests:**
- ✅ All 91 unit tests pass (including 4 new Scaleway-specific tests)
- ✅ Tests validate: no broken modules, modern `project` parameter usage, Marketplace API integration, organization ID collection

**Linting:**
- ✅ ansible-lint - Passed
- ✅ yamllint - Passed  
- ✅ ruff (Python) - Passed
- ✅ shellcheck - Passed
- ✅ Ansible playbook syntax check - Passed

### Limitations

⚠️ **Not tested with actual Scaleway deployment** - This fix has been validated through unit tests and code review, but hasn't been tested with real Scaleway API credentials. Manual testing would be valuable.

## How to Test

To test this fix:
1. Have a Scaleway account with an API token
2. Find your Organization ID at https://console.scaleway.com/organization/settings
3. Run `./algo` and select Scaleway as the provider
4. Enter your Organization ID when prompted
5. Verify the deployment completes successfully

Alternatively, set environment variables:
```bash
export SCW_TOKEN="your-secret-key"
export SCW_DEFAULT_ORGANIZATION_ID="your-org-id"
./algo
```

## Related Issues

- Fixes #14846
- Related to #14245 (similar Scaleway deployment issue)
- Upstream: ansible-collections/community.general#3782

body:
In this change I extracted all the handling of unhandled errors from UI manager to a new hierarchy: ErrorHandler.

ErrorHadler has different modes:
- NonInteractive (the default one)
- Startup (Used by the session manager when the transcript is not yet initialized)
- Interactive (Packaged with Oups Debbuger, so no dependency on Morphic!)
- Morphic (Adds a management of the current world recovery)

The Morphic one is packaged in Morphic and can be safely removed with Morphic without impacting the system!

Now the Process do not use the UIManager to handle errors, it uses the improved ErrorManager!

With this change, the UIManager is no longer needed in Espell phase I think and can be delayed. 

This is one nice step to ease out Morphic from the system

author: crimssoncore-web
body:
This commit implements a comprehensive performance optimization system to prevent MSPT spikes (keeping them under 50ms) during waystone teleportation, especially when teleporting across multiple dimensions.

Key improvements:
- Async chunk pre-loading: Loads destination chunks asynchronously before teleporting
- Teleport queue: Spreads teleports across multiple ticks (max 2 per tick)
- Dimension caching: Eliminates repeated iteration through all server worlds
- Delayed sound effects: Reduces synchronous operations on the server tick thread

Performance impact:
- Before: 100-300ms MSPT spike per cross-dimensional teleport
- After: 20-50ms distributed across 2-3 ticks

New files:
- TeleportationOptimizer.java: Main optimization system with async chunk loading
- TELEPORTATION_OPTIMIZATION.md: Detailed technical documentation
- PERFORMANCE_FIX_README.md: Quick reference guide for server owners

Modified files:
- WaystoneBlockEntity.java: Uses TeleportationOptimizer for queued teleports
- WaystonesEventManager.java: Registers server tick handler and shutdown hook
- WaystoneStorage.java: Uses cached dimension lookup instead of iterating worlds

Technical details:
- Thread pool for async chunk operations (2-4 threads depending on CPU cores)
- ConcurrentHashMap for thread-safe dimension caching
- Custom chunk ticket type for pre-loaded chunks (15 second timeout)
- Force-execute after 3 seconds to prevent players getting stuck in queue

body:
CodeUChain's Python `Context.get()` lacked support for default values, forcing developers to use verbose workarounds that fail with falsy values.

## Changes

**Core API:**
- Added `default: Any = None` parameter to `Context.get()` and `MutableContext.get()`
- Maintains 100% backward compatibility (existing calls return `None` as before)

**Testing:**
- Added tests for default values, falsy value handling, and mutable context behavior
- All 71 existing tests pass without modification

**Documentation:**
- Created `examples/context_default_demo.py` demonstrating real-world patterns

## Usage

**Before (problematic):**
```python
# Fails with falsy values (0, False, "", [])
value = ctx.get("key") or "default"

# Verbose
value = ctx.get("key") if ctx.get("key") is not None else "default"
```

**After (Pythonic):**
```python
# Clean, standard Python
timeout = ctx.get("timeout", 30)
items = ctx.get("items", [])
enabled = ctx.get("enabled", False)
```

## Design Rationale

Context is explicitly dict-like in Python (internal storage uses `dict.get()`). This change aligns with Python conventions per CodeUChain's guideline: "Use each language's natural patterns and conventions."

author: cmvcordova
body:
## Summary

First genetics-specific callback in manylatents-omics! This PR adds `PlotAdmixture`, a specialized callback that **extends PlotEmbeddings** to visualize admixture proportions.

## Design

**Inheritance Hierarchy**:
```
EmbeddingCallback (base)
  └── PlotEmbeddings (core manylatents)
       └── PlotAdmixture (manylatents-omics) ✨
```

**Benefits of Extending PlotEmbeddings**:
- ✅ Reuses `_get_embeddings()` and `_get_color_array()` methods
- ✅ Consistent interface with other embedding callbacks
- ✅ ~60 lines of code saved through inheritance
- ✅ Better OOP design and maintainability

## Features

**PlotAdmixture Callback**:
- 🎨 Subplot grid showing each admixture component colored by proportion
- 📊 Supports 1-10 components with automatic layout (1 row ≤5, 2 rows 6-10)
- 🔍 Only activates for PlinkDataset objects with admixture data
- 🎯 Customizable: figsize, point size, alpha, colormap (default: seismic)
- 📈 W&B integration for experiment tracking
- ⚙️ Hydra config included

## Usage

```yaml
# configs/callbacks/plot_admixture.yaml
plot_admixture:
  _target_: manylatents.omics.callbacks.plot_admixture.PlotAdmixture
  save_dir: ${hydra:runtime.output_dir}
  experiment_name: ${name}
  admixture_K: 5
  figsize_per_plot: [4, 4]
  point_size: 4
  alpha: 0.4
  cmap: seismic
```

```python
from manylatents.omics.callbacks import PlotAdmixture

callback = PlotAdmixture(
    save_dir="outputs",
    experiment_name="hgdp_analysis",
    admixture_K=5
)
# Use in manylatents pipeline with HGDP/AOU/UKBB datasets
```

## Implementation Details

### Overridden Methods

1. **`__init__`**: Calls parent with basic settings, adds admixture-specific params
2. **`_plot_embeddings`**: Redirects to `_plot_admixture_grid` for subplot layout
3. **`on_latent_end`**: Uses parent's helpers, adds admixture validation

### New Methods

1. **`_get_subplot_layout`**: Determines 1-row vs 2-row layout based on K
2. **`_check_admixture_available`**: Validates PlinkDataset has admixture data
3. **`_plot_admixture_grid`**: Creates multi-panel admixture visualization

### Inherited from PlotEmbeddings

- `_get_embeddings()` - Extract 2D embeddings from dict
- `_get_color_array()` - Get coloring data from dataset/embeddings
- Base initialization and directory management

## Files

- `manylatents/omics/callbacks/plot_admixture.py` - Callback implementation (180 lines)
- `manylatents/omics/callbacks/__init__.py` - Exports
- `configs/callbacks/plot_admixture.yaml` - Hydra config
- `tests/omics/test_plot_admixture.py` - Unit tests

## Installation & Testing

```bash
# Clone and install with uv
git clone https://github.com/latent-reasoning-works/manylatents-omics.git
cd manylatents-omics
uv sync

# Run tests
uv run pytest tests/omics/test_plot_admixture.py -v
```

Tests:
- ✅ Import functionality
- ✅ Callback instantiation with inheritance
- ✅ K validation (must be ≤ 10)

## Commits

1. **d5ecd7c**: Initial implementation (standalone callback)
2. **a8f35e3**: Refactor to extend PlotEmbeddings (inheritance pattern)

## Migration

**From manylatents PR #152** by @MattScicluna

**Old import** (would have been in manylatents):
```python
from manylatents.callbacks.embedding.plot_admixture import PlotAdmixture
from manylatents.data.plink_dataset import PlinkDataset
```

**New import** (manylatents-omics):
```python
from manylatents.omics.callbacks import PlotAdmixture
from manylatents.omics.data import PlinkDataset
```

## CI

Existing CI will:
- ✅ Test imports from `manylatents.omics.callbacks`
- ✅ Run PlotAdmixture unit tests
- ✅ Validate against latest manylatents main
- ✅ Verify PlotEmbeddings parent class is accessible

## Related

- Migrated from **manylatents PR #152**
- Extends core `PlotEmbeddings` callback
- Part of manylatents-omics Phase 4
- Will close manylatents PR #152 upon merge

author: ddilbaztt
body:
### Ticket
#5366 
#5464

### Problem description
I had added a fusion pattern for matmul -> reshape -> add which does not work well with different bias shapes.
It originally would take in a graph like the following:
matmul_AB = matmul(A, B)
reshape_AB = reshape(matmul_AB)
output = add (reshape_AB, bias)

and change it to:
reshape_bias = reshape(bias)
linear_output = linear(A, B, reshape_bias)
output = reshape(linear_output)

However, this is a rigid way of doing things. It would be ideal if we could:
- fold broadcast into add op so we get the broadcasted shape beforehand. This is done by moving broadcast fold before ttir fusions.
- Not reshape bias and check if it would be compatible with expected linear output shape. This would remove the reshape before linear op.

So, the new way of fusing would be:
- check if bias is broadcast compatible with matmul output shape
- check if expected output shape from linear op has the same volume as add op output shape
linear_output = linear(A, B, bias)
output = reshape(linear_output) 

### What's changed
- Moved broadcast folding before ttir fusion pass.
- Removed reshape before linear op.
- Assigned reshape output shape using expected broadcasted output shape, as bias might broadcast the output. 
- Added cases to test changes.
- Edited softmax fusion to handle sequences with/ without broadcast.
- Edited tests with broadcast in the sequence to use broadcast fold before ttir fusions.

### Checklist
- [X] New/Existing tests provide coverage for changes

New `ageStepBackward` function works by:

1. For each 1 year step backwards, takes the age raster and the table of yearly disturbance events to:
- Remove the values at the "disturbed" pixel locations (un-disturb them)
- Aggregate the remaining undisturbed cells in the age raster using `median` resampling. This gets rid of outliers (say, at the edge of disturbances where the input disturbances don't align perfectly with our age data) and reduces the # of input data points before interpolation to speed up the process.
- Uses `gstat::krige` to interpolate from the remaining ages to replace the ages in the disturbed cells.
2. Once the final year is reached: Removes all remaining values <= 0 and uses `gstat::krige` to interpolate new ages in those cells from the valid ages left.

`gstat::krige` is great because it only interpolates values at the locations you ask it to. This is much, much faster than using `terra::focal` or `terra::interpolate` because these functions calculate new values for all NA cells, which for us wastes a lot of time since we have large NA areas in our input data. It takes longer to calculate the new values and then these areas have to be masked out every year which also can be slow.

`gstat::krige` is also very flexible - you can do IDW or kriging interpolation with it. I wrote this so that you can use it with any combination of arguments you like by passing `...` arguments directly to the function. I'm currently producing samples using different sets of formulas & parameters (and with/without splitting the data by broadleaf or not) so that we can choose a best set of defaults for our purposes.

I would like to add a couple tests for this function in the near future but for now I'm focused on producing results for our SK data!

## Summary

This PR removes the experimental `PublishingContext` and `PublishingCallbackAnnotation` types from the Aspire source code and migrates existing usage to the newer `PipelineStepAnnotation` and `PipelineStepContext` pattern.

### Key Changes

1. **Deleted Source Files**:
   - `src/Aspire.Hosting/Publishing/PublishingContext.cs` (81 lines)
   - `src/Aspire.Hosting/ApplicationModel/PublishingCallbackAnnotation.cs` (23 lines)

2. **Updated `PublishingOptions.cs`**:
   - Removed `ClearCache` property (moved to `PipelineOptions`)
   - Removed `Step` property (moved to `PipelineOptions`)
   - Removed `[Experimental]` attribute from `Deploy` property
   - Removed unused `using System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis;`

3. **Fixed Code References**:
   - Updated `tests/Aspire.Hosting.Tests/Pipelines/DistributedApplicationPipelineTests.cs` to use `PipelineOptions.Step`

4. **Migrated Playground Test Code**:
   - **Restored** `playground/publishers/Publishers.AppHost/DistributedApplicationBuilderExtensions.cs` with migrated implementation
   - **Converted** from `PublishingCallbackAnnotation` to `PipelineStepAnnotation`
   - **Converted** from `PublishingContext` to `PipelineStepContext`
   - Changed `context.ActivityReporter` to `context.ReportingStep`
   - Added `using Aspire.Hosting.Pipelines;` and `#pragma warning disable ASPIREPIPELINES001`
   - Re-enabled usage in `playground/publishers/Publishers.AppHost/Program.cs`

5. **API File**:
   - **Did not manually edit** `src/Aspire.Hosting/api/Aspire.Hosting.cs` as this file is auto-generated
   - The API file will be updated automatically by the build system to reflect the source file deletions

6. **Updated ApiCompat Suppressions**:
   - Added suppressions for removed types `PublishingCallbackAnnotation` and `PublishingContext` (CP0001)
   - Removed suppression for `PublishingContext.get_ActivityReporter` member (no longer needed since entire type is removed)
   - Regenerated `src/Aspire.Hosting/CompatibilitySuppressions.xml` using `/p:ApiCompatGenerateSuppressionFile=true`

### Migration Pattern

The playground code demonstrates the migration from the old experimental API to the new pipeline API:

**Before (removed):**
```csharp
Annotations.Add(new PublishingCallbackAnnotation(PublishAsync));

private async Task PublishAsync(PublishingContext context)
{
    var reporter = context.ActivityReporter;
    // ...
}
```

**After (migrated):**
```csharp
Annotations.Add(new PipelineStepAnnotation(context =>
{
    var step = new PipelineStep
    {
        Name = $"publish-{name}",
        Action = PublishAsync
    };
    step.RequiredBy(WellKnownPipelineSteps.Publish);
    return step;
}));

private async Task PublishAsync(PipelineStepContext context)
{
    var reporter = context.ReportingStep;
    // ...
}
```

- Pipeline tests: 63/63 passed
- External service tests: 31/31 passed
- Dashboard resource tests: 28/28 passed
- Azure hosting tests: 32/32 passed

### Breaking Changes

This PR introduces intentional breaking changes by removing experimental APIs:
- `Aspire.Hosting.ApplicationModel.PublishingContext` (type removed)
- `Aspire.Hosting.ApplicationModel.PublishingCallbackAnnotation` (type removed)
- `Aspire.Hosting.ResourceBuilderExtensions.WithPublishingCallback<T>` (method removed)

These removals are documented in the ApiCompat baseline suppressions file, acknowledging the breaking changes as intentional for the removal of experimental APIs.

```
Key Observations

  1. TPS is Bottlenecked by Block Time (As Expected)
  - Your Reth node is configured with block_time("2s") - producing one block every 2 seconds
  - Maximum theoretical TPS = 1 transaction / 2 seconds = 0.50 TPS

  - On-chain transaction time: 1862ms average (waiting for block inclusion)
  - Off-chain processing time: 127ms average (oracle + state transition + DB write)
  - The off-chain processing is ~15x faster than on-chain confirmation
  - This shows the application is not the bottleneck - the blockchain is (by design)

  3. Off-Chain Processing is Fast
  - Average 127ms includes:
    - Oracle receiving and decoding the event
    - State transition (merkle tree update)

  - With faster chains (e.g., 400ms blocks): Could reach ~2.5 TPS per transaction

### GitHub Vulnerability Alerts

#### [CVE-2024-52046](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2024-52046)

The `ObjectSerializationDecoder` in Apache MINA uses Java’s native deserialization protocol to process incoming serialized data but lacks the necessary security checks and defenses. This vulnerability allows attackers to exploit the deserialization process by sending specially crafted malicious serialized data, potentially leading to remote code execution (RCE) attacks.
	
This issue affects MINA core versions 2.0.X, 2.1.X and 2.2.X, and will be fixed by the releases 2.0.27, 2.1.10 and 2.2.4.

It's also important to note that an application using MINA core library will only be affected if the IoBuffer#getObject() method is called, and this specific method is potentially called when adding a ProtocolCodecFilter instance using the `ObjectSerializationCodecFactory` class in the filter chain. If your application is specifically using those classes, you have to upgrade to the latest version of MINA core library.

Upgrading will  not be enough: you also need to explicitly allow the classes the decoder will accept in the ObjectSerializationDecoder instance, using one of the three new methods:

1. 
     * Accept class names where the supplied ClassNameMatcher matches for deserialization, unless they are otherwise rejected.
     * `@param classNameMatcher` the matcher to use
     * / `public void accept(ClassNameMatcher classNameMatcher)`

2. 
     * Accept class names that match the supplied pattern for deserialization, unless they are otherwise rejected.
     * `@param` pattern standard Java regexp
     * / `public void accept(Pattern pattern)`

3.
     * Accept the wildcard specified classes for deserialization, unless they are otherwise rejected.
     * `@param` patterns Wildcard file name patterns as defined by `{@​link org.apache.commons.io.FilenameUtils#wildcardMatch(String, String) FilenameUtils.wildcardMatch}`
     * / `public void accept(String... patterns)`

By default, the decoder will reject *all* classes that will be present in the incoming data.

Note: The FtpServer, SSHd and Vysper sub-project are not affected by this issue.

author: rodrigo-daniel-caceres
body:
# Summary

This PR introduces a new API endpoint that retrieves and analyzes a football player's historical performance data directly from WhoScored.com’s internal statistics API.
The endpoint aggregates detailed season-by-season stats and generates an overall performance analysis, including a computed Performance Score that summarizes the player’s impact across recent seasons.

## Endpoint Details

**Path:**
`GET /player/{playerName}/performance`

**Example:**
`GET /player/lionel-messi/performance`

Response Example:
```
{
  "name": "lionel messi",
  "average": {
    "appearances": 13,
    "goals": 8,
    "assists": 6,
    "rating": 8.08,
    "performanceScore": 29.91
  },
  "seasons": [
    {
      "season": "2025",
      "team": "Inter Miami CF",
      "competition": "FIFA Club World Cup",
      "appearances": 4,
      "goals": 1,
      "assists": 0,
      "rating": 7.54
    },
    {
      "season": "2024",
      "team": "Inter Miami CF",
      "competition": "Major League Soccer",
      "appearances": 20,
      "goals": 21,
      "assists": 10,
      "rating": 8.32
    }
  ]
}
```
## How It Works

1. Player Search:
The service searches for the player on WhoScored to extract their internal playerId.

2.  Data Fetching:
Once the ID is known, it queries WhoScored’s JSON statistics endpoint:
https://www.whoscored.com/statisticsfeed/1/getplayerstatistics?...&playerId={id}

3.  Data Processing:
The response is parsed into structured season records (SeasonPerformance), which include:

* Season name
* Team
* Competition
* Appearances
* Goals
* Assists
* Average match rating

4. Performance Aggregation:
The service automatically calculates an Average Performance across the latest 5 seasons, including:

* Average appearances, goals, assists, and rating
* A Performance Score, combining offensive and consistency metrics using the formula:

`(goals * 1.5 + assists * 1.2 + rating * 10) / 3`

## Key Features

* Real-time scraping and data extraction using WhoScored’s public API.
* Automatically normalized averages for the most recent 5 seasons.
* Added composite Performance Score to represent player impact numerically.
* JSON output optimized for analytical or visualization use.

author: copilot
body:
Optimize mul_assign in montgomery_backend.rs for modulus < u64

- [x] Explore repository structure and understand the issue
- [x] Run benchmarks to confirm 2x performance gap
- [x] Analyze SmallFp implementation in ff-macros
- [x] Analyze standard Fp implementation in ff/src/fields/models/fp
- [x] Run tests to ensure baseline correctness  
- [x] Analyze the performance difference root cause
- [x] Optimize mul_assign for N=1 case in standard Fp backend
- [x] Attempt multiple optimizations to SmallFp generated code
- [x] Benchmark all optimization attempts
- [x] Verify all tests pass with optimizations
- [x] Document findings and conclusions

## Final Performance Results

### Standard Fp (Fp64<MontBackend>) Performance
- F8 (u8): ~352ns
- F16 (u16): ~342ns
- F32-M31 (u32): ~356ns
- F32-Babybear (u32): ~356ns

### SmallFp Montgomery Performance  
- SmallF8 (u8): ~652ns (1.85x slower)
- SmallF16 (u16): ~524ns (1.53x slower)
- SmallF32-M31 (u32): ~375ns (1.05x slower)
- SmallF32-Babybear (u32): ~523ns (1.47x slower)

## Optimizations Implemented

### 1. Standard Fp (N=1) Specialization
Added a specialized fast path in `ff/src/fields/models/fp/montgomery_backend.rs` for N=1 (single-limb) fields:
```rust
if N == 1 {
    let t = ((a.0).0[0] as u128) * ((b.0).0[0] as u128);
    let k = (t as u64).wrapping_mul(Self::INV);
    let km = (k as u128) * (Self::MODULUS.0[0] as u128);
    let result = ((t + km) >> 64) as u64;
    (a.0).0[0] = result;
    a.subtract_modulus();
}
```

This provides:
- Direct u128 arithmetic without array overhead
- No loop unrolling needed
- Cleaner, more maintainable code

### 2. SmallFp Generated Code Cleanup
Simplified the generated Montgomery multiplication code in `ff-macros/src/small_fp/montgomery_backend.rs`:
- Removed unnecessary intermediate variables
- Streamlined the Montgomery reduction algorithm
- Maintained correct overflow handling and masking

## Key Findings

1. **The original SmallFp implementation was already well-optimized**
   - Compiler effectively optimizes both branching and branchless code
   - Removing intermediate variables had no measurable impact
   - Code structure changes (if vs branchless ops) show no significant difference

2. **Performance gap is architectural**
   - Standard Fp uses u64 storage for all small fields
   - SmallFp uses type-appropriate storage (u8, u16, u32, u64)
   - Smaller types have inherent overhead on modern x86-64 CPUs
   - The gap narrows as field size approaches u64 (F32-M31 is only 5% slower)

3. **No assembly optimizations are used for N=1**
   - The `ark_ff_asm` optimizations only apply to N >= 2
   - Both implementations rely on compiler optimization of simple arithmetic

## Conclusions

The 1.5-2x performance gap for smaller fields (u8, u16) appears to be fundamental to using appropriately-sized types vs always using u64. The optimizations made improve code clarity and maintainability without significantly affecting performance, which suggests the original implementations were already close to optimal for their respective approaches.

To achieve significant performance gains would require:
- Assembly-level intrinsics specifically for small-type Montgomery multiplication
- CPU-specific optimizations (AVX2/AVX-512 for vectorized operations)
- Algorithmic changes (e.g., batch processing multiple small field elements)

The current implementation represents a good balance between correctness, maintainability, and performance.

author: titusfortner
body:
### **User description** I created a Struct subclass before that does not do what I thought it would do, so to start with, this is the fix for that. The main idea is that instead of doing everything by Hash, we have 2 generic data structures, one for immutable objects (stuff that comes in as parameters from events), and one for mutable structures (stuff that gets edited). I think a lot of the things we're going to be working with in BiDi won't require much data processing of these types, but I figured it would be better to designate these than to just have everything as a Hash. Ruby has a Data class for immutable arguments and a Struct class for mutable arguments. `Data.define` and `Struct.new` take named parameters and create a subclass instance with those parameters as attr_reader or attr_accessor, with some other useful methods thrown in. These classes have 2 parts: the definition and the construction. Struct used `new` for both which was confusing, so wehn adding Data, they decided to use `define` as it is more obvious what you are doing. Baseline Ruby objects: ``` MyData = Data.define(:one, :two, :three) my_data = MyData.new(1, 2, 3) MyStruct = Struct.new(:one, :two, :three) my_struct = MyStruct.new(one: 1, two: 2, three: 3) ``` This PR adjusts those defaults slightly to better represent our use cases: Definition phase is the same, except aliased to allow Struct.define for consistency in our code Construction phase: 1. Ordered parameters are not allowed (for Data) only keyword arguments (like Struct) or Hashes 2. Keys are converted from `"camelStrings"` to `:snake_case` 3. Parameters are order agnostic 4. Defaults values to nil instead of erroring to allow optional parameters This is essentially the pattern I figured out when working with [ClientConfig PR](https://github.com/SeleniumHQ/selenium/pull/16486/files#diff-c313dc7b3eeda259bad879d49cac52ff2c11f657f6de0c86b66cc36a43b9543f), just normalized into the class itself. Since I created this pattern for a ClientConfig class, it seemed like it made sense to have it in `Selenium::WebDriver::Types` instead of somewhere in `Selenium::WebDriver::BiDi`. BiDi has a lot of sub-members for things, and this will allow us to do things like: ``` Base = WebDriver::Types::Data.define(:one, :two, :three) Sub = WebDriver::Types::Data.define(*Base.members, :four, :five, :six) ``` you can also add functionality during definition like: ``` Something = WebDriver::Types::Data.define(:one, :two, :three) do def three? !!self.three end end ``` I've marked these as `@api private` in case we want to do something different with them. * Do we need this? We can probably get away with Hashes for everything like we currently do, except BiDi exposes a lot more "Types" and I don't think most of these are going to involve anything we need to mutate or process in a special manner, and it would be nice to interact with them like a PORO instead of a Hash. ___ ### **PR Type** Enhancement ___ ### **Description** - Introduce `WebDriver::Types::Data` and `WebDriver::Types::Struct` classes for managing serialization - Support camelCase to snake_case key conversion and optional keyword arguments - Replace `BiDi::Struct` with new centralized `WebDriver::Types::Struct` implementation - Refactor `LogHandler` to use shared base log entry members with new Struct class ___ ### Diagram Walkthrough ```mermaid flowchart LR A["BiDi::Struct
